You must be Patricia. Dan Brooks, I run the Marietta plant. How was the flight?
Long. Ten hours, and I still do not know what time my body thinks it is. Have you ever been down to São Paulo?
Twice, years ago. Enormous city. My wife still talks about a churrascaria we went to and I still cannot pronounce the name of it.
Then you have eaten better than most people here. Can I ask you something? Do you know whether the Marietta team is on the monthly people call?
Two of them are. I am not, which is probably a mistake. You are the one who wrote the note about the first ninety days, aren't you?
I am. I was wondering if you would have twenty minutes while I am here. Marietta is the site I understand least.
Sure. Swing by tomorrow after ten, I am in the building all day. Fair warning, I will tell you that most of it is the shift pattern.
Then we already agree on something. Thanks for the heads-up -- I will see you tomorrow.

People from outside the US think small talk is a waste of four minutes. It is not four minutes of nothing, it is four minutes of finding out how to talk to you. In that time I am working out how direct I can be with you, whether you want to be asked about your family, whether you are the kind of person who answers a question with a joke, and roughly how senior you feel. All of that changes how I run the next fifty minutes. So if you skip it, I do not think you are efficient. I think I have no idea who I am talking to, and I get more careful, not less. The other thing to know is that nobody expects the answer to be interesting. How was your weekend is not a request for information. It is a handshake with words, and the only wrong answer is silence.

Three things, and I got all of them wrong for about a year. The first is that I answered questions completely. Somebody asked how the project was going and I gave them four minutes. They wanted twenty seconds and a door to walk through. The second is that I waited to be invited. In Brazil somebody senior brings you in. Here, if you want twenty minutes with the plant director, you ask the plant director, and nobody thinks it is strange. I lost most of a year waiting for an introduction that was never coming. And the third one still catches me. When an American says we should grab lunch sometime, that is not a plan, it is a friendly noise. If you want the lunch, you have to say which day. Say Thursday. They will say yes or they will say Friday. Either way you have a lunch, which is more than I had in my first year.
